findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes resource IDs with group IDs and cannot find per-group resources
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then both looks up permissions with hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the result set. This is wrong on two counts: (1) per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, clientId) with the group id as the resource NAME and a store-generated ID, and without setting the resource type, so findByType("Groups") never returns them; (2) hasPermission resolves resources with findByName(...), so passing a resource's generated ID as a 'group id' finds nothing and falls through to the all-groups type resource. Consequences: an admin holding only per-group view-members/manage-members grants gets an empty set, so the UserModel.GROUPS filter used by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource user search and getUsersCount is never applied at the DB level — searches scan all realm users and rely on the in-memory canView filter, which breaks pagination (first/max are applied before filtering) and returns wrong counts. Worse, an admin holding a view-members/manage-members grant on the type-level 'Groups' resource gets that resource's UUID added as a bogus 'group id', so user search and getUsersCount return zero users even though canView(user) evaluates to true. The existing tests pass only because the in-memory usersEvaluator::canView filter compensates; nothing covers the all-groups or paginated cases.

findings.title: canManage() (no-arg) grants manage rights for a view-only permission on Groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the global, no-argument variant) falls back to hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. a caller granted only the 'view' scope on the Groups type resource passes the manage check. requireManage() (no-arg) guards POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup), which both creates top-level groups and, when the representation carries an existing group id, moves that group to the top level via realm.moveGroup. So an admin explicitly granted only 'view' on Groups can create groups and move arbitrary existing groups. The per-group variant canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE only, as does UserPermissions.canManage() for the Users resource; the no-arg variant should not accept VIEW. The javadoc added in GroupPermissionEvaluator matches this code, but the behavior contradicts the method's contract and the per-group semantics.

findings.title: UnsupportedOperationException thrown on live code paths (group deletion, management-permissions endpoints)
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, viewPermission, etc. to throw UnsupportedOperationException, but these methods are still invoked on real paths when the V2 feature is active. AdminPermissions.registerListener (guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag, which can be enabled together with — or implied by — ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on every GroupRemovedEvent, so deleting any group in a V2 realm throws UnsupportedOperationException and the DELETE fails with a 500. Similarly GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled call isPermissionsEnabled(group)/getPermissions(group) after ProfileHelper.requireFeature(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which now returns 500 instead of the previous working V1 behavior (before this change MgmtPermissionsV2 fell back to the functional V1 GroupPermissions implementation). Either these paths must be guarded/disabled for V2 realms or the V2 implementation must handle them instead of throwing.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions realms never get the Groups resource or the new group scopes (no migration)
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Realms where the admin permissions client was already created (e.g., with the earlier Clients resource type support) will therefore never receive the new 'Groups' type-level resource or the new group scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) that init() creates from the schema. In such realms, creating any group scope permission fails: getOrCreateResource does scopeStore.findByName(...) for each schema scope and throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when a scope is missing, and getScope rejects the request with "Scope [...] does not exist". Additionally getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups") returns null because the type resource was never created, which makes GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission fall into the null-resource path. A migration (or lazy creation of missing type resources/scopes for existing admin-permissions clients) is needed; otherwise upgraded realms cannot use the new Groups resource type at all.

findings.title: hasPermission can NPE when the 'Groups' type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when the per-group resource is not found the code assigns resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) without a null check, then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes(). getResourceTypeResource returns null whenever supportsAuthorizationSchema is false — e.g., the realm's admin permissions flag is disabled while the admin permissions client (and its resource server) still exists, or the 'Groups' type resource is missing in a pre-existing realm (see the init()/migration issue). In those states, any group permission evaluation (canView(group), requireView(group) on GET /groups/{id}, etc.) throws a NullPointerException instead of denying access. A null check returning false is needed. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission, but GroupPermissionsV2 is newly added by this PR.

findings.title: No test covers user search/count with a type-level (all-groups) permission or pagination under group-scoped permissions
findings.body: The new tests only exercise user search for admins holding per-group view-members/manage-members grants on a single group in a realm with two users, where the in-memory usersEvaluator::canView filter masks any problem in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. There is no test for: (a) an admin holding view-members on the type-level 'Groups' resource performing user search/getUsersCount (this currently returns zero users because the resource UUID is used as a group id); (b) pagination/first/max correctness when the DB-level group filter is absent or wrong (currently searches scan all users and filter in memory); (c) getUsersCount with group-scoped admins. Adding these would catch the broken group-id enumeration in GroupPermissionsV2.
